subject: Quantive Health — inference runway & tokens/sec headroom plan
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Marie Larson <marie.larson@quantivehealth.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 2 Feb 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Quantive headroom proposal — tokens/sec and SLO note

Hi Marie — great to chat yesterday. Per our conversation, attaching a concise runway estimate + two capacity options so Quantive can align procurement timing. High-level numbers below; full calc attached (quantive-runway-calc.xlsx).

Summary (workload assumptions)
- Model variants: decoder-only base (quantized) for 95% traffic; larger instruct variant for 5% (longer context).
- Avg request size: 18 tokens in prompt, 120 tokens generated (conservative).
- Peak QPS target (application): 8 requests/sec sustained, 20 rps bursting for short windows.

Token rate estimates
- Sustained tokens/sec = 8 rps * 138 tokens = 1,104 tokens/sec (t/s)
- Burst tokens/sec = 20 rps * 138 tokens = 2,760 t/s

Latency/SLO mapping (target p95)
- Target p95: 350ms across 95% of requests. Using our quantized decoder path we map 350ms p95 ~= 900 t/s per A100-equivalent slab under 8-concurrency batching (empirical).

Recommendations (two options)
1) Minimal Dedicated slab (cost-efficient): Reserve 2 A100-equivalent slots to cover sustained load with 30% headroom for average day-to-day (2 * 900 t/s = 1,800 t/s) — covers sustained 1,104 t/s and short bursts with fallback to hosted autoscale for peaks.
2) Committed burst-ready pool (SLA-backed): Reserve 4 A100-equivalent slots (3,600 t/s) to provide native headroom for 2,760 t/s bursts with ~30% cushion for KV cache cold-starts and tail variance.

Ask: can you confirm whether Quantive needs native handling of the 20 rps bursts without a hosted fallback? That determines whether we recommend Option 1 + hosted burst vs Option 2.

Next steps: I attached the detailed calc and a short PDF summary. If you want, Priyom can walk Quantive's SRE through the p95 tail assumptions and cache warmup behavior.

Thanks — Ben

Ben/Laura — quick technical confirmation and recommended phasing. See inline bullets.

Cold-start / KV warmup
- Empirically for similar alert patterns we observe a KV-hit warmup window of ~120–240s after an extended idle (depends on model context reuse). During that period effective throughput capacity can be 20–30% lower until caches are hot.

p99 tail and headroom math (alert path)
- Alert path: 20% of traffic; if overall sustained is 8 rps, alert path sustained = 1.6 rps; bursts = 4 rps (during peak). But customer says alert path can spike to 20 rps in short bursts — we treat that as local burst scenario.
- Using our profiling: quantized decoder slab yields ~900 t/s nominal p95. p99 tail headroom factor ~1.8x vs p95 under realistic queueing (so effective p99 capacity per slab ≈ 900 / 1.8 ≈ 500 t/s).
- For alert burst of 20 rps with 138 tokens avg → 2,760 t/s. Required slabs for p99-native = 2,760 / 500 ≈ 5.5 → round up to 6 slabs to keep p99 < 800ms consistently.

Recommendation (final)
- Phase 1 (commit now): Reserve 3 slabs (A100-equivalent). This covers sustained plus p95 target with ~35% day-to-day headroom and keeps committed spend reasonable while we onboard. Pair with hosted-burst billing for rare long tails.
- Phase 2 (month 2–3): Move to 6 slabs reserved if Quantive confirms no-hosted-fallback for alerts. 6 slabs give native p99 headroom for 20 rps alert spikes and reduce per-token cost compared to hosted bursts.

Notes on mitigations
- We can add route-based throttling/priority: pin alert traffic to dedicated priority pool to preserve capacity, while lower-priority inference spills to hosted fallback during extreme peaks.
- Encourage KV pre-warm policy for scheduled quiet windows (run a 5–10 minute warmup before business hours) to avoid cold-start deficit.

I'll attach an updated calc sheet and a one-pager for procurement. If this looks good I can draft the committed-capacity SKU and phasing language for procurement by EOD Monday.

— Priyom
